newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton seen stable in Pakistan, firm in India.
newsitem.headline: Cotton seen stable in Pakistan, firm in India.

text.p: Cotton prices are likely to hold steady in Pakistan next week but firm in India due to a shortage of good quality stocks, dealers said on Friday.

In Pakistan, rates were unchanged on Friday with spinners showing little interest, said dealer Abdul Qadir Kashan at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said. He said rates were unlikely to shift much before the new crop starts arriving at ginneries by the end of this month.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was quoted at 2,125/2,250 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), K-68 at 2,425/2,450 and MNH-93 at 2,425/2,450.
The KCA said Pakistan had shipped 74,224 bales by May 28 out of 110,304 booked for export, compared to 1.815 million and 2.32 million respectively in the same period a year ago.

Pakistan's state-run Cotton Export Corporation (CEC) said on Friday that 1996/97 (July-June) cotton output had reached a provisional 8.77 million 375-lb bales by June 12, down from 9.95 million in the year-ago period.

In India, cotton prices gained due to a shortage of quality cotton on the local market, dealers said. The shortage of ready stock resulted from dwindling arrivals at producing centres as the 1996/97 season (Oct/Sept) drew to a close.
Dealers said most of this season's crop, estimated at 16.78 million 170-kg bales, had arrived in the market.
"Whatever is left with farmers will also come into the market with the onset of monsoon this month," said Chandulal Thakkar, a leading cotton dealer.
The four-month June-September monsoon arrived in the southern state of Kerala about a week later than usual.
Spot Bengal-deshi rose five rupees to 1,050/1,080 per maund and Punjab saw-ginnned by 20 rupees to 1,850/1,900. F-414 gained 20 rupees to 2,060/2,080.
Among Gujarat varieties, Kalyan cotton rose 200 rupees to 14,500/15,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Wagad cotton gained 300 to 13,400 per candy.
Last week the government permitted a state-run agency to export 100,000 bales. "The move to export cotton also helped market sentiment," Thakkar said.
Traders said global cotton yarn prices, which were high last month, had now come down sharply.
"This will mean demand from spinning mills for cotton will not be as good as it was some time back," Thakkar said.
($1 = 40.49 Pakistani rupees)
